Resource: FHIR Version: R4B (4.3.0) — base resource: DiagnosticReport. NEW PROFILE — identified as a critical gap from real handover data (investigations.12-Lead ECG showing ST elevation was completely unmodeled).

Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Canonical FHIR ValueSet (required binding): registered | partial | preliminary | final | amended | corrected | appended | cancelled | entered-in-error | unknown. FLAG FROM REAL HANDOVER DATA: the source system's investigations.status value 'collected' does not map cleanly to any of these — 'collected' describes specimen state, not report state. Recommend mapping vendor 'collected' → 'registered' or 'partial' (result pending) and reserving 'final' for when an actual conclusion/result is attached, as in this sample where a conclusion is already present despite status='collected' — clarify this mapping with the vendor, it looks like an inconsistency in their source data.

Description: Broad diagnostic service category, e.g. cardiology (CG) for an ECG.
The specific investigation performed. Maps to investigation_id/investigation_name, e.g. LOINC 11524-6 '12-Lead EKG panel'.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. The sample payload's investigation_id ('LOINC-11524-6') is correctly LOINC-based, consistent with the vitals guidance elsewhere in this workbook — reuse as-is rather than re-coding.

Description: The patient the investigation was performed on.
The encounter this investigation was performed in — typically EMPOCEncounter, or a downstream ED Encounter.
When the investigation was performed/recorded. Maps to recorded_at.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT — as time-critical as vitals for protocols like STEMI, where door-to-ECG and ECG-to-activation intervals are actively measured.

Description: Who performed/recorded the investigation. Maps to recorded_by.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — recommended to always populate in practice.

Description: Free-text clinical interpretation, e.g. 'ST elevation in leads V1-V4; consistent with anterior STEMI'. Maps to notes.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — this is the single most clinically urgent field on this profile in the STEMI example; must never be silently dropped or truncated during ingestion. Preserve verbatim.

Description: Coded equivalent of the free-text conclusion, e.g. a SNOMED CT code for 'ST elevation myocardial infarction'.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..*) — strongly recommended to populate alongside the free-text conclusion (not instead of it) so downstream systems (SHA claims, cardiology alert dashboards, quality reporting) can query structurally rather than parsing free text. This is what should trigger, e.g., a STEMI-activation alert automatically rather than relying on a human reading the narrative.

Description: Discrete measurements underlying the report, if captured separately (e.g. specific ECG interval measurements).
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support. Most field EMS ECG capture will only have a narrative conclusion, not discrete measurement Observations; populate opportunistically if the device/software provides them.

Description: The actual ECG trace/waveform image or PDF, if transmitted alongside the report.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support on this profile, but genuinely valuable when available since a receiving cardiologist will often want to see the actual trace, not just the narrative conclusion.
